transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, my family brought me in. See, I was at the county fair, giving a talk... and I just climbed right up onto one of the tractors they had on display. I kept jerking the controls around, trying to show the crowd this... this new pattern I figured out. People were yelling at me to get down, but I just couldn't make myself stop.
Have you ever had periods in the past—before this week or this month—when you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing?

Yeah, I have. Especially with the sleep. There's been times where... well, most nights I'll only sleep maybe two or three hours, usually just sitting in my chair. Or sometimes I don't sleep at all. But then I'm up way before the sun, feeling completely charged. I just get ready to work the place like nothing happened.
Besides these energetic periods with little sleep, have you ever had times when you felt very depressed, down, or hopeless for several days or longer?

No, I can't really say that I have. I mean... sure, farming is a hard living, and you get frustrated if the weather doesn't cooperate or something breaks down, but... no, I don't get down or hopeless like that. I've never really been the type to just sit around feeling sad for days on end. I just keep focused on what needs doing around the property.

During these times when you're feeling very energetic and sleeping very little, have you ever experienced anything unusual—like seeing things that others couldn't see, or believing things that others told you weren't real?

Well, yeah, I suppose so. Um... during those months when I was hardly sleeping at all, just pushing the farm expansion day and night, things got... strange. I started hearing voices coming from the irrigation lines. Clear as day. And I was looking at my yield maps, and I started reading these warnings in them. Like a code. People told me it was just stress or I was making it up, but... I saw what I saw, and I heard what I heard.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a manic episode with psychotic features. Key diagnostic features include: (1) distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated/expansive mood with increased goal-directed activity (climbing tractor, farm expansion project), (2) markedly decreased need for sleep (2-3 hours nightly, feeling 'completely charged'), (3) racing thoughts and increased talkativeness (giving talks, elaborate plans), (4) psychotic symptoms occurring during the mood episode (auditory hallucinations from irrigation lines, delusions of reference in yield maps), (5) no history of depressive episodes reported, and (6) significant functional impairment and behavioral disinhibition (inappropriate public behavior at fair). The presence of psychotic features during a manic episode, rather than as a primary psychotic disorder, and the absence of a bipolar depression history point to F30.2 (Manic episode with psychotic symptoms) as the primary diagnosis.
